title: Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. Media Availability | Wednesday, October 7th | Press Conference
text: Um I guess I guess just uh you know we spoke to you not long ago but uh when you've gone back and looked at the film uh you know what were your big takeaways I guess from the game? >> Um man it's just great to see the team play complimentary football. Um feel like early on when we got the ball uh started the game. Um didn't that drive didn't end the first drive didn't end how we wanted it to. just some small mental errors that we had to overcome as as a offense, you know, but and then uh for the defense to uh go out there and we we get a um we get a a strip whenever the defense strip the ball and now we got ball in field position. For us to go out there and put seven points on the board, that's awesome to be able to see that. And obviously our special teams been playing remarkable um all all season. So it it's been good just all all phases of the ball. I know that you have confidence in in all your guys, but when when it comes to Drake, um you know, he's he's the kind of guy that really anything you toss up almost at any point, he's going to come down and get. What is your level of confidence with a guy like that? >> Yeah, I mean, you're very confident, you know, uh when you have a guy where it's like it's either his ball or nobody's, you know? Um so it's it's awesome to be able to have that on a team, you know, but um yeah, like you hinted on it. Um, I'm comfortable with everybody, but yeah, Drake, um, he he's definitely been playing some really good football for us. >> Between the run game you guys have, the line you guys have, is there less on your plate? Like, do you feel like they're alleviating pressure off of you and you can kind of play a little bit more free if that makes sense? >> Um, I mean, it's we're doing whatever it takes to win football games and, uh, and I feel like each and every week we come in with a great run plan. So, you know, we always have a great run plan, obviously. Um, you know, Coach Callahan, he he's one of the best out there if if not the best, you know, to do it, you know. So, to be able to have somebody like that in offensive line room that's helping us with our run playing stuff, you know, it's definitely going to um help help the pass game as well. So to to what you're saying, yes, I mean, all everything is it takes more than, you know, just one specific thing that that can help elevate, you know, you're talking about my play and uh the things that's on my plate, but it it's still a lot on my plate as well, too. You know, with the run game, all our cans, and you know, just making sure I'm I'm locked into the details and stuff like that so that I can get us into the right run so that we can uh be successful. So So >> of the runs you guys had, how many did you actually have to check into last week? Um, >> I don't I can't say a number. It's It was probably It was quite a few. It was quite a few. >> Yeah. >> Your responsibility in this system more than it was in the last two years. Do you control more at the line of scrimmage? >> Uh, I wouldn't say it's more or less, you know. Um, I wouldn't say it's more or less to be honest. And each each week, you know, it's it's different. You know, each week you I might have I might have more more can plays that I have have than the week before. So, it's it's always different. >> What's the process like of starting over? You know, you put one game plan together, you come back in. I guess y'all start start that on Wednesday morning. >> Yeah. For for you, what is when does it start? Does it start Tuesday evening? >> Yeah, for sure. It it started it started on Tuesday. You know, I'm watching the film getting ahead of it so that whenever we did come in uh today, um you know, I already have an idea of of why why we're we have the plays in that we have, you know, um for the normal down and distance stuff. So, >> is that the first time you see sort of the plays you're going to be running that week is Wednesday morning? >> Um, yeah, usually. Yeah, Wednesdays. >> How would you characterize uh Drake's competitiveness? >> Uh, I don't know. It's unlike any any other, you know. I I feel like that that is a mindset, you know, and for him to have that mindset, that dog mentality, you you hear that get thrown out a lot, you know. It's it's a mindset. It's still a want to do it, you know, and not and for him it's like, okay. Yeah, you see that dog mentality whenever he has the ball in his hand or the ball that's coming his way, but he also has it whenever it's not, you know, and it's in a run game, whether he has to block, you know, he has to, you know, help open somebody else up in the um pass concepts, you know. So, it's it's about the mindset and then um not just not being selfish about it, but you know, obviously trying to help other people be successful as well. >> I know we're dealing with a short sample size, but you've completed like almost 75% of your passes so far. Do you think that that's based on the system? Do you think that you're found that you're structurally throwing the ball better than you have been? Is that just the way it's gone two weeks? >> Uh, I just say just the operation, just operating at a high level and um just trust trusting myself, you know, trusting my feet, making sure my feet and my eyes are tied together um to to make all the throws and obviously, you know, um scheme and all that stuff has stuff to do with it as well. Obviously, you know, um because we're setting a lot of things up with our run pass, you know, options. So, it's it's definitely it's a combined of all those things. >> Are you surprised you feel this comfortable in it right away? I mean, cuz this is your first live action in this system and you look like you've been doing it for a while. >> Yeah, I wouldn't say I'm surprised. You know, I put the work in, you know, and I'm going continue to put the work in and, you know, I feel like it's I got I got a long ways to go. I feel like I could be so much better. There's a couple passes in the game, especially this game that pass, you know, that uh I wish I I could have back, you know. So, it's it's always it's always, you know, room for improvement. So, I'm always looking to get better. >> You look like you're seem like you're having fun. You seem like you're you're happy. I know you get on the way and good stuff going on, but how much how good do you feel playing right now? >> Yeah, I feel great. I feel great. Um, you know, it's awesome to to be able to see the team, you know, um, all buying in and, you know, just trusting the process. Obviously coming off of uh the first two losses, you know, it was the team to to be able to see the team, you know, whenever you get two losses early like that, you know, some teams can, you know, just sit there and like, you know, soak into that and, you know, not not really have that energy. But for the guys to, you know, still come with that same energy every day, that competitive mindset to want to go out there and get better each and every day, it helps elevate everybody, you know. So, it helps elevate my play, it helps elevate uh Bjan's play, everybody that you see in making all these plays. It's because of the energy and the culture that we we have here and just the the will to want to win. So, >> how do y'all turn uh the stadium into a home field advantage? >> You got to show up, man. We need all our fans to show up. Um we're super excited, you know, to be back home. Obviously, we we've been away uh these past couple weeks. So, um super excited to be back in front of our home crowd and obviously a prime time game. So, we can't wait to see everybody uh pack out the bins. And uh the Ravens when you game playing, what did you see on their defense there? >> They got some players, man. They got some ball players. They're they're a really good team, you know, all around, but definitely, you know, just talking to uh defensively, you know, I feel like they they have guys everywhere. You know, their their front is good and they got backers that's good, defensive backs as good as, you know, it's hard to find a weak point in their defense, you know, but you know, we got to we got to just lock into our scheme and trust our scheme. And I know that the coaches, they'll make sure we we have all the right things uh prepared for us so we can come out and be successful again. >> What did you see from Roco on the defense? >> Oh, yeah. He's uh he's a leader, you know, he he's the one that make all that thing go uh make that whole defense go. So, it's to to see him out there, you know, he he's definitely a very good player. He's been playing for for a while. I think um about nine years now. I think this is year nine for him. Um but yeah, he has a lot of experience, you know, played a lot of football and he he's definitely somebody that uh keeps the keeps them going. >> And they move Kyle around um a lot. What do you have to kind of you kind of know what they're trying to do, where you can locate him? >> Yeah, for sure. He's a ball player as well, you know. Um man, he he he's going to make plays. We're going to make plays, know, but um we're excited for the challenge. We're excited for the challenge. >> I believe you were you might not even been in high school yet when Tommy was playing college quarterback. Do you remember watching him at all? Have you gone back and watched him play quarterback? >> No, I don't I don't remember watching him. I need to go back and look at it. >> What's he like in a meeting room? >> Uh he's great. You know, he's great. He's um just his communication is awesome. You know, he makes sure that, you know, all the plays that we look at, he's giving giving us a reason why he's calling it, you know, and letting us know our outlets and things things like that so that we can go out there and play fast. So, it's been really good. I know Zach was also kind of along those lines or is younger, played QB in college, but how much does it does it help you to have a coordinator who who actually played QB at a high level? >> Um, wait, what were you saying? You talking about Al uh D? >> No. Does having Tommy? I mean, Zach was also, you know, I think he played at Okay State. >> Yeah. Yeah. In his day, >> he was balling in college. >> Yeah. Does it help you to to have a coordinator who can maybe who has played, you know, he played QB, he kind of understands it through like the way you view it as well, I would imagine. Yeah, I mean that's that's a tough question because like I said uh Zro Rob, you know, he he played at a high level in college as well, you know. He he was balling at Oklahoma State, you know. Um but same as Tommy as well, but um to to your point like just having a quarterback, somebody that's played the position. Absolutely. It helps because they they understand the game, they understand, you know, um it's not always like, oh, why didn't you do this? It's, oh, they've been in your shoes before, so they they might know. So it's definitely um it's very good to be able to have somebody that play the position. Tommy's got some great uh Pressbox camera clips up there. Do y'all uh >> I seen one of them. Yeah, I seen one of them. I just saw it like couple couple days ago. >> You did. Do y'all give him grief about those or >> No, we we mentioned it to him. Um that was about it. He just laughed it off. >> That was a Notre Dame one. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. >> Have you heard that phrase before? >> No, I haven't heard that one yet. [laughter] >> That's probably a good thing. Yeah, you're doing your job. >> Yeah. Let's not Let's not hear that one. Anything else? >> I appreciate y'all. >> Thank you, Mike.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Tuesday, October 6th | Press Conference | LIVE
text: Okay, good to see you guys. Uh, obviously great effort last night. Got to watch it on the airplane and uh, pleased in a bunch of different areas. U, just like I mentioned last night, I thought execution was at a high level. U, you know, across the board obviously to go into an environment like that versus a football team and and come away with a win. Uh, speaks to how the guys put the work in that week. Uh, so excited about that and then go from a long week to a short week. So, great opponent coming to our place on Sunday night and uh we got to quickly move on and and quickly put a game plan together and then see the guys tomorrow and install that game plan. But um injury front, I don't really have many updates for you guys just yet. Uh we'll get those over the next 24 hours and work through that those type of things this week and I'll keep you guys posted. But with that, I'll take any questions. >> Go to Mark Zeno. Kev, obviously the run game the last two weeks has been amplified and not that it was bad the first two weeks per se, but what are you seeing that has been so much more successful, not only last night, but the last week that has elevated in the run game and why it's been so much better? >> Well, kind of like we talked about, I think last night, Mark, is when everybody's doing their job, you got a chance. And when everybody does their job and then you have talented runners like Bjon and Brian, they don't need a a big hole. You know, you can give these guys creases and they can run through arm tackles and uh you know, that's that's at your success is when you got all 11 doing their job. Having said that, uh these are tough outings and and tough defenses that you're going against. I know this week is is certainly no different going up against Baltimore. Uh you really have to be on point uh to have success in the run game versus teams like Baltimore. Joe Patrick. >> Yeah, Kevin, these last two weeks, Mike has, you know, been the quarterback and had to go into some some tough situations with Lambo that being their home opener there and obviously everything that was in the Superdome last night. Are you surprised by just how composed he's been in in in these performances and in his ability to to operate this this offense? >> Yeah, Joe, I'm really not. And I say that because uh obviously getting to know Mike over the last few months and just talking to coaches that have been with him previously here, that's kind of who he is and and that's what you want in a quarterback is the ability to uh you know stay even keel through these tough games and through a tough quarter or a tough play. And like you mentioned, these are difficult places to play. They they make life hard on you when you're trying to communicate in the huddle at the line of scrimmage. So, uh, that's part of playing this position is operating and I thought Mike has done a nice job operating. >> Joe, go again. >> Yeah, it al it also looked just sticking on Mike that he was willing to take some hits um, you know, kind of willing to stand in there and hit some shots downfield. Is is that an him him advancing kind of in this progression coming back and and being able to see him stand in there and take that? I I think it's a good question I think to ask Mike. I I just that's how he's played the position his whole life. That's how you have to play this position. There's some moments that that you have to stand and deliver. Uh and I think Mike gets that. >> Yeah. Coach, on the rewatch uh on the plane, how did uh Jerel grade out there? >> Yeah, I thought Mike played a good game deled. I thought, as you know, when you go into these games as a swing tackle, you have to be ready to play left, have to be ready to play right. So, I thought he was uh ready to go. Uh are there things we can clean up? Absolutely. Uh that's why why we work, that's why Coach Callahan uh works these guys and and and we will clean them up. But I thought in in a tough situation with a great rusher, I thought he did a nice job. >> Thank you, Joe. Uh Kevin, um with these rookies that you're getting so much production, especially these guys on on the defensive side of the football, what what do you attribute them being able to step in and contribute so quickly to? >> Well, as we've talked about over the course of time here, there's no red shirt years in in the NFL and and you're counting on your rookies to play. And I think this is a a very diligent group of rookies and have been from day one since they've been here. uh whether you don't really care who you're talking about when you're talking about these this rookie class that they they're all about business, they're about their ball. Uh and as coaches, we appreciate that because there's so much work that goes into this and there's so many uh things behind the scenes to get ready to play a game like the one last night and just what what we do in the meeting room, what we do on the grass, uh just to get our our bodies ready. I think these guys understand uh and and are starting to understand what it takes to be a pro. Park Zo >> Kevin, I know everybody was focus focusing on the offense, but I really liked what you said after the game last night about, you know, how you run and how you stop the run uh being, you know, a quality quotion of what kind of football team you are. The run defense has been outstanding. What are the keys to it and why has it been successful? Well, I I think big picture there's things about schematics and and I think you know, Coach Brick and our defensive staff does an excellent job in putting these game plans together and I think the guys are understanding what we're asking of them. And then at at another level, it's about being just physical and beating the man across you and getting off blocks and and there is a mentality part of playing defense where you have 11 hats on the football and I think that's that's what we preach. Uh and that's what the guys do out there. Again, these challenges week to week are are not easy and and I know it's not going to be easy with with a great rush attack, great offense coming into our place on Sunday night. Uh these are huge huge huge challenges and and we got to give our guys a game plan to go execute and the guys have to come through. Eli. >> Uh yeah, coach, with the um you know, we saw Jake last year just battle through a high ankle and you know, just kind of got a army to keep him out off out of the game out of the game. But with a groin, how do you have to try to you know, manage that if you know with an older guy that you know, you don't want that kind of thing to linger? I would guess. >> Sure. We'll be smart. I I don't have enough information yet to say, you know, what this week looks like. Uh, I know Jake will battle like crazy to make it. Uh, we'll work through it and and we'll make sure that we make, uh, good decisions for the football team. >> Thank you, >> Joe Patrick. >> Uh, I haven't checked the full snap counts, but it looked like Kyle Pittz wasn't playing much early in the game. I was just kind of curious as to why his his usage was what it was last night. >> Yeah, I I think week to week game plan wise, uh, we'll continue to rotate guys in there. Kyle obviously made some plays for us last night which he will continue to do. >> Mark Zo, >> Kev, kind of forgive the nature of this question because it's not meant, you know, for you to to talk badly about any one player or anything, but like just when you objectively when you watch the offense the last two weeks versus the first two weeks, everything just looks like it has more flow. It looked more continuous. It looked more in sync. like is there anything that beyond just the switch of Cooper to Mike that you have done or made changes into that has made things much more effective and efficient? >> Yeah, I'm not going to get into specifics. Uh we just uh we'll focus on on what we're doing week to week. Obviously uh pleased with the performance last night, but you don't carry these things with you. So we have to be better uh going into next week. Darius, >> Kevin, um, with this long home stretch coming up, um, how crucial is it for you guys, um, knowing that you have this really long stretch of games at home in front of your fans? >> Well, you know, we we love playing in front of our fans, obviously. U, we're so focused on on the next one, I can't really tell you what comes after that. Uh, but anytime we get to play in front of our fans at the Benz, it's pretty special. So excited about the opportunity this week. >> Yeah. And Kevin, this is just to kind of understand the thought process here or or what was happening, but it looked like there was an opportunity to potentially challenge a Saints catch that may have been incomplete kind of lateish in in that game. I think it was Vle who caught it. And I'm just curious if you had seen a replay at that point in time or if you just decided with the lead you would rather just kind of save the challenge. Just kind of curious what the what the process was there. Yeah, all those type of decisions. You're you're taking all that into account, Joe. And uh I think you have to also understand that replay assist gets involved in these things and and they can overturn them if it's clear and obvious and and if they don't, then you have to be pretty uh diligent or smart about if you're using your your challenge there. So, uh, I I'm very comfortable with the communication we have on game day, very comfortable with with the information I'm getting, uh, down there on the sideline, and we'll continue to operate as such. >> Anybody have anything else? >> All right. >> Okay. Appreciate you guys, guys. >> Appreciate it. >> Thanks, coach.

title: Reaction to Ravens' Trade for Cam Jurgens | Baltimore Ravens
text: [music] Welcome into the lounge. I'm Ryan Mink here with Garrett Downing and we have big trade news to report. The Ravens have traded for Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens. According to ESPN's Adam Shfter, the Ravens gave up a second round pick in the 2028 NFL draft and fifth round pick in 2027 in return for Cam Jurgens and a seventh round pick in the 2027 NFL draft. This is a big time move for this team. The Ravens find their long-term replacement for Tyler Linderbomb and in the short term a player that they badly need after three centers have landed on the injured reserve to begin the year. Yeah, I think that this is a move. The Ravens are looking at their team. Eric Das is looking at their roster and saying, "We're three and one right now, but what's the biggest area of need?" And it's clear that center is at the top of the list. That was a need and a priority for the Ravens going into the off season after Tyler Lindbomb left in free agency. And then to top that off, the Ravens have an incredible series of bad fortune with three centers going down with major injuries in training camp in the early part of the season. So, you immediately find yourself in this deep hole that you need to try to climb your way out of. Well, enter Cam Jurgens, two-time Pro Bowler from the Philadelphia Eagles, one of the best centers in football. Now, you get somebody that can come in and make an immediate difference on your offensive line. And also, you have him for the long term. Like, this is a move that's going to benefit this team right now and for the foreseeable future. All right, so we're going to talk about who Cam Jurgens is, as well as what those short-term and long-term ramifications of this trade are. And so, let's just start first with who Cam is. This is a second round pick out in Nebraska who was really drafted and groomed to be Jason Kelce's replacement in Philadelphia, the seventime Pro Bowler, Jason Kelce. And so, he started his career really at right guard. Was a starter there for a season in 23. Then Jason Kelsey retired. He moves into the center position, which they always felt like was his best position. Then went back-to-back Pro Bowls. He was so good in the 2024 season that the Philadelphia Eagles signed to a four-year extension. After just one year as a starting center, they signed him to a 4-year 68 million extension before last season. So that kind of tells you a little bit about his background and how highly the Eagles thought of him. Now, this season, he started as their starting week one center, but then Landon Dickens, Landon Dickerson, their starting left guard, went down with an injury. So, the Eagles move Cam Jurgens to left guard, a position he's never played before. It's been a little bit of a struggle. It's been a struggle for their entire offensive line in Philadelphia. Then, oh, by the way, this week, Lane Johnson, who will probably be a Pro Bowl right tackle someday, or I'm sorry, a Hall of Fame right tackle someday, he announces his retirement. And so, now they've got the retirement of Lane Johnson. They've got Lander Dickerson down. Their offensive line is really kind of moving pieces on the go here and and uh struggling. So, they offload Cam Jurgens to the Ravens. Yeah, look, Cam Jurgens had that the really challenging assignment of stepping in for a legend. Like, that's always a tough job when you're the guy that's following the legend. And Jason Kelsey was a legend. Uh he might be a Hall of Famer in his own right at center. And Cam Jurgens was the one that followed him. And he went to the Pro Bowl his first season as a starter in replacement of Jason Kelce. He allowed them to do some of the things that they were so well known for, most notably the tush push. Uh he's one of the guys that is really the leader, the literal tip of the spear on that play. And and then he played really well last year, too. Again, back-to-back Pro Bowl seasons. And then this year, he's got versatility, too. Now, the Ravens plan for him to be the center. He's going to be he's going to be the center to be the center, right? >> Just to be clear on that. He's played both guard positions and center, but he's going to be a center for this team. But the versatility certainly doesn't hurt. It's nice that you have that as an option, but yeah, he's going to be the starting center for this team. Uh, one note on him is he is coming off of a concussion in the last game, so he's got to get cleared from that. uh before getting back in the lineup. Reports uh from Adam Shepard are that he's not expected to play this game, but will make his debut a week from now when the Ravens take on the Cleveland Browns on the road. >> Well, he's also got to get up to speed with the playbook and all that stuff. I mean, we're Wednesday the Ravens just announced his trade. I assume he won't be here probably till later today, tomorrow, so there's a lot from a mental standpoint, too, that he's got up to speed with. You know, Landon Dickerson recently did an interview this week where he said he really felt bad uh for Cam Jurgens that he had to play out of position, play a position he's never played before, you know. So, I think now it's a return to where he fits best. It's a a really good player who is going to instantly upgrade this offensive line because of all the injuries. It allows Venga Yawwan now to move back to his natural position at right guard which is where you know Venga played great against the Titans stepping in at center but he's a right guard you want you want Venga to be able to flourish and develop there right so this gives you a really strong interior totally uh in totality and then Cam Jurgens also 27 years old so let's talk about the long >> well just just in terms of this year with Yana sliding back to right right guard this just made your offensive line better at two positions Yan gets to go back to his natural spot at right. You elevate the center position by adding a Pro Bowl center. It's been hit hard with this season at center and at guard. Andrew Vorhees went down last game with a foot injury. So, it's been hit hard with injuries. But for this discussion, let's just assume good health here for the offensive line. I want to talk about good health for this offensive line after they've dealt with a number of injuries this year. But if you go Ronnie Stanley Johnson, >> Ronnie's dealing with a toe injury. He is, but like he played last game and hopefully this is something that the Ravens can put behind him and move past it. So you have Ronnie Stanley, John Simpson, Cam Jurgens, Van Gawan, Roger Rosenard. I feel really good about that offensive line. Like you have Pro Bowlers at at at center and at left tackle. You have a rookie first round pick that's impressed everybody at right guard. You have a veteran proven commodity uh at left guard and John Simpson. And I really like Roger Rosenarten on the right side and I think that he's had a good start to the season. Absolutely. Look, this was a move the Ravens have been looking for the replacement for Tyler Linderbomb. Really off season, all offseason. They tried to resign Tyler, right? Couldn't didn't make it happen. The Raiders blew the top off the market with a deal that averaged $27 million annually, right? So, tried to get him back, but didn't. Tried to draft the Tyler Bomb replacement in in the draft, but they all went before the Ravens expected them to. So, then they pivoted. They signed three ultimately veteran free agents. They went out and got Danny Pinter, Javon Gwyn, and Ethan Posix. Now, all three have gone down with injuries. So, the Ravens have been really trying to kind of solve this center problem for months now, and they just did it, right? They aggressively did it. And coming out of last season, certainly the top thing that we was everybody's to-do list was upgrade the interior offensive line. You look at this, trading a second round and fifth round picks to do it. Using a first round pick on Venge Yuan and signing John Simpson to a three-year reported $30 million contract. >> Pretty big moves to upgrade the interior of this offensive line. >> Yeah, no question about it. And I think it also shows that Eric Tas and the Ravens want to be aggressive. They know that this team sitting at 3 and one has championship aspirations and beliefs that they can get there. And in order to to get to that level, to be one of the best teams in the league, they know they their offensive line has to play well. And having a a rookie play out of position for the long term for throughout the season was really not something that they wanted. It's just like if you want to be at your best, that's not like the alignment and the way that you want to approach the rest of the season as just like your solution. Especially even when you then add in the fact that now your backup right guard is also hurt in Vorhees with a foot injury. And so it's like you're down to your fourth string center and your third string right guard in week five. That's not a good situation. So like for all those reasons, it just makes a lot of sense. And I think that the what the Ravens gave up giving up a second and 28 reportedly and a fifth next season in return for Jurgens and a seventh rounder next season. I think that that shows like they they were willing to pay a steep price because this was a position that something they they felt like was necessary and they know how good this team is and how good it can be and they needed to make a move there. >> Well, everybody knew that the Ravens were needing a center, right? That was that much was clear after you have three guys lay on IR, right? And so, but but I look at what the price that the Ravens paid. A to your point about aggressiveness, the Ravens tried to to strike a deal for Max Crosby this past offseason, right, which was two first round picks. Like not afraid to be aggressive. Eric Daza is in aggressive mode right now, right? Then I also look at it like this is the most aggressive deal that they've executed since Rocoan Smith. They dealt a second and fifth round picks for Rocoan back in 2022. Yeah, >> that deal, that trade has definitely worked out. Roan's become a centerpiece of this defense, a leader. Exactly what you want. I expect Cam Jurgens is going to be the same thing. And so, I think that the Eric Dasa is certainly showing that he's willing to take big swings to improve this team. Doing it now as opposed to waiting till later, closer to the trade deadline, gives you more Cam Jurgens, you know, just more games that he can play in. And I I I also give him credit for I think a lot of us looked at this center problem and said nobody's training you starting centers. Nobody's going to give up a starting center. Maybe when you get to the trade deadline when teams feel like they're out of it and they go into seller mode. >> Well, not only do the Ravens strike a deal for a starting center, it's a Pro Bowl starting center. >> He's one of the best. >> He's one of the best. But he's he's attacked his rehab. Um he's been such a positive guy and I'm just I'm excited that he's able to come back out for him. >> What's it like game playing against a quarterback that's so good pre- snapping Joe Burrow? Yeah, it's a challenge and um you know I think he's you know one of the top top guys in the league. He can make all the throws. He's smart. He sees it all. He can get in and out of the right calls constantly at the line of scrimmage. I just I have so much respect for how tough he is and how he sits in and takes shots and holds on and makes throws when guys are coming right at him and keeps his eyes down the field. you know, last year I didn't get a chance to go against him because he was injured when we played them, but just studying him on film for the last two years, I I just I think he's he's one of the top guys in the league, and I I love the way that he plays. And I think it also helps that he's got some premier weapons around him. Um, some of the best receivers in the league. I think Chase is at the at the very top after we played them last year and I saw him live. I have a ton of respect for him. um complete complete route runner, great hands, great body control, can catch and run, is strong, is willing to block. I just I think he plays the game the right way. And then obviously they have Higgins and a very athletic tight end and a and a good capable back who I think runs really really hard and he's good in pass protection and they've got a good old line. They've got they've got a lot of talent. Um so it'll be it's always a challenge to go up against a quarterback like that with some weapons. Um, you know, I'm looking forward to it. >> We're almost at the one quarter mark of the season. Regarding Malik Willis, I'm wondering how you evaluate him. What can our guys handle going into a game plan? How many calls can we execute? And it's, you know, that's always when you get a new group of guys, it's always something you really have to look at and work with and communicate. And um you want to see progress as you go. Is that a concern? We know that Malik is a work in progress. Is that a concern or you're just >> I I would say like everything else like what what can we do better, right? We got to look ahead at this point and not behind and we got to improve. Um, and that's with everything that we're doing right now in all three phases with with all the coaches and all the players and and that's where we're at. >> With Austin, obviously there there's been some struggles that we attributed to the caliber opponents that he's faced, but uh, at what point do you get concerned about how he's performing and how it's impacting the offense? >> I'm not concerned. I think if you really study that tape and watch the tape, you'll see improvement from Austin in that last game as well as the rest of our offensive line. Um, so I am not concerned. >> Have what do you see in the run game overall this season? Um, like essentially the last two games without Devon Han, but you rushed for 119 then 121. You had a 31 31 carries two games ago, which are positive things. Where is the run game? What have you seen >> about the run game? um in back-to-back weeks has shown signs of improvement. The problem last game was we ran 37 plays. I mean, you don't get a lot of opportunity to get at bats to run the ball. We have to sustain drives. We have to get off the field on defense and get more opportunities to play offense. Um so, that's a team, offense, defense, and special teams. But I think we're capable to run the football. Our offensive line, I think, has improved across the board. I think they're getting better. Um, and and I'm excited to see that as we go throughout and excited to see it this week. I think their interior is really good. Um, probably the best interior Dline that we've played against, and they got some edge guys, multiple guys that can rush. I think their front seven's really good. So, I think this is a challenge the offensive line, and I think they're excited for it. This is a good front that we're playing. I know, you know, we just spoke, you know, Omar about playing certain really good players right on the edge. I think this is a really good defensive line. >> How's Jaylen Ray doing? >> Jaylen's good. Yeah. >> How did he perform? >> Um, you know, again, he didn't get he didn't get many attempts, you know. Um, but I'm I'm excited to see him going forward. He's going to, you know, he had a good week of practice last week coming back, you know, after, you know, um, being out a little bit, but I'm excited. I thought he had a good week and we'll see what he can do this week with more plays. >> When it comes to Ali, we always talk to him and he seems like a fun guy to be around. What's he like behind the scenes, especially with how he stayed ready for for this opportunity? >> Yeah, probably just like you see him. He's very upbeat. He's got a big personality. He's a very positive person. Kind of lights up a room when he walks in. Um, I've seen growth as far as how he's practicing, though. I think he's matured on the field. Um, you know, even last week I complimented him after one of the practices how when he gets the ball, he's going full speed and he's not stopping and he's taking it past the area we tell him he could stop and he he's running about 30 40 more yards. Um, I think his practice habits, I think his the way he's hand handling teammates and talking to teammates, I think he knows now the role he's in, he's got to grow in a lot of areas and he is and he's still young. Um, so we'll see how it goes. >> What do you feel has been the biggest issue in terms of defending tight ends? >> Um, what do you mean in what do you mean by that? Like you want me to get >> numbers the opponent's position? >> Yeah. I I think I think you have to look in terms like this is how I view defense. All right. When you go into each game, who do you want to stop? Is there a wide receiver you want to stop? Is there a run game you want to stop? Is there a quarterback you have to stop? Can the quarterback run the ball? Right? So, you got to kind of pick and choose when you go into a game. If you have an elite receiver, right, and we're going to say we have to really focus on that guy to make sure he doesn't beat us because your quickest way to get beat a lot of times is with these elite receivers and getting the ball thrown over your head and not paying a lot of attention to him. Is it a run game? Are they going to try to run the ball 30 times? Do we have to load up the box and be really aggressive in certain situations in the run game? Um, and then is there a quarterback that can run the ball that we have to keep an eye on him in case he breaks out? You can't do it all. So, some games it might be the tight end, some games it might be the wide out, some games it might be the running back. So, I kind of look at it game by game. And that's how I've always been on defense. So, I don't look at it like, oh man, this week the tight end had this many catches for this many yards. It's, you know, what do we need to do to keep the points down to help us win the game? And that's how I've always coached. Some weeks it's the running back. we're going to have to load the box and we're going to have to do everything we can to stop the run. Um I I just I don't I don't look at it in that regard. I look at it big picture of what we need to do to win and keep points off the board. >> Quick follow up if I may. Is there ever a time where you would look at the opposing offense and go the tight end is the guy we have to stop? >> Absolutely. Yeah. If he's the most explosive player and we need to pay attention to that guy for sure. But just in general, when you look at a team, it's who do we have to stop that can beat us the fastest and you kind of go down in that order or who do we need to protect on our side of the ball that they're going to go after, right? So, I think that all kind of balances out as you go. I mean, if you want to look at this week, it's there's there's a couple guys that we're gonna have to pay very close attention to, you know, and you can't pay attention to all of them. So, I respect the question and you know, there's some plays we need to play better on tight ends in situations where we're right there and there's some where they might get a five yard pass cuz in zone defense there's a no cover zone that they're dumping the ball off to and you're rallying that there's give and take. Does that make sense? >> Speaking of tight ends, [clears throat] Captain America is high in snaps last week. Things he's doing to impress you would like >> Yeah, I think it's his physicality in the run game that's probably the best. Um there's multiple times where I've showed clips where he's just getting after people and putting them on their back. He had the nice catch early on in the game. He had a chance for another one. I just think he we just missed it. Um so I just I see the development as a you know a young player. He's getting better. >> Can you speak on Chubs Robinson's mindset because obviously he's coming off this sack. He led the NFL in pressures in week four and we all have our opinions of what happened in week three against Kansas City Chiefs. just his performance, right? What he did this week for. Can you just speak about that? >> Yeah, he he's confident and you know, I talked to him about it last night. He's he's getting into a rhythm and he's playing again and he's playing fast and he's practicing fast and he understands that how he prepares is how he's going to play and and that was really the topic of our conversation. I wasn't surprised he played well because of the way he practiced. Now, can he do it again? Like that's the challenge. Can he go out and practice that way to give him a chance to play the same way he did? Because if he doesn't, he won't, right? So now it's time to put the pressure. I got it. Congrats. You had your 10 pressures and your sack. I love it. But can you do it again? Because if you don't, then it doesn't matter. And the only way to do that is to come out today and have the best practice he's had all year. Because now people are going to be watching him and they're going to be trying to get after him a little bit. Just like we talked about a tight end, there's going to be some teams that say, "I'm not going to let Chop have a sack." And it might open it up for somebody else. That's how our game works. So, he's got to go out today and he's got to have a great practice. But, I love this guy's attitude. I love the way he practices. I love the way he works. He is totally bought in. Um, and I just I'm excited for the guy. >> How's Douglas doing since we last spoke and will practice? >> He will not practice today. Um, I would say he's still one day at a time. He's getting better. Um, but it's just it's just not there today. half. Kind of building off of what you said about your defensive mind and somebody on the other team that you've got to stop flipping it. How do you think defensive coordinators look at your offense without Devon Han? Who do you think they think we've got to stop him? >> That's a good question. Um I think you answered it pretty clearly. When we had, you know, 28, it was probably to stop him. I would say right now um they're probably looking at the strength of our offensive line and what we were still able to do in the last two weeks running the ball and I'd say that's probably what they're looking at, but it's probably a better question for you to ask Hal Golden. Um so if you want to call him up and ask him how he's going to plan to stop us, I'm all for it. >> I will share it with you. >> I appreciate you get on their Zoom today. Going back to Chop, you mentioned um in the preseason, I think it was uh during the spring, uh that you want to see him come up become a complete player this year. Um where is he as far as that trajectory? What it was the best player I've ever been around when you turn on the tape. Like when a guy has a really good game, we don't need to tell him he had a good game. Everybody Everybody's telling him he had a good game. He knows it. Our job is to turn tape on and challenge him in the areas where he he needs to improve and push him when he's feeling good. I mean, that's my job is when they're feeling good, it's my turn to kind of push him and to make sure that they stay on it and get better, right? Because there's certain things, whether it's his first step, whether he can tighten up his stance, where are his eyes, you know, can can he still improve in his physicality in the run game? like all the little things that he's getting better at to continue to challenge him cuz he can be a complete player, but we have to coach him and continue to develop him like all these players. Um cuz one good game, can you do it again? I mean, that's all cuz that's what you have to do in this league. >> Speaking with the defensive line, you guys obviously got a lot of pressures in that game. Was there an unsung hero to leading T? Is it coverage on the back end just great individual efforts that open things up for someone else? When you watch the tape, was there a group of you that said like this linked to why we saw this result? >> It's it's how you play like it's how you play team defense. It's rush plus coverage. It's the guys in the back end are doing their job and they're where they're supposed to be cuz even on that first sack on the first play of the game, Kyler went to throw the ball into an area where we had disguised, which was great job from the safeties and we were in a cloud. So he went here thinking he'd have free access based on what we showed and he had to step and rehitch and something was coming back and by the time he stepped and rehitched Sealer had made a play and we were right in his face. So it's those guys over there did a great job which bought them an extra click to get the sack. So that to me that's team defense. That's how we need to play. We're our style is going to be playing together where one benefit fits from the other. The unsung hero in the game is Jordan Phillips because the statline is never going to be like as much as a Chop Robinson. But when I turn on the tape and there's three guys blocking him and he's still throwing them off and he's making a play or there's three guys blocking him. So now Rodriguez has 18 tackles, right? Like those are the unsung heroes of the game. The guys doing the dirty work that are grinding on double teams and getting 650 pounds on them the whole entire game. Like that's not fun and you don't get rewarded for it. Like that's what's fun about defense. It's totally everybody has to be on it. >> Spoken a lot about how Chris Johnson can be successful outside and inside. His snaps are actually about evenly divided. Um is there an advantage to having the slot be a guy who doesn't come off the field? Is that your preference for some strategic reason or is it is it just happened to [clears throat] work out this way this year? Yeah, that's a good question. Um, it can be an advantage, but as you go throughout the game, I think, you know, people kind of figure out who's subbing in and what we're getting into. I think there's some packages where it hides a little bit and he's always on the field and they might not know where he is going to be. Um, but I really do believe that, and we've seen it the last two weeks, he's really good inside. I mean, he is physical and how how physical he was with those wide outs last week who I thought were good blockers and had a lot of respect for and he blitzed a couple times off the edge which forced some really bad throws. Um, I think it's hard to do as a rookie and I told you guys since the beginning. I think I knew he had it in him and he still we need to still coach and develop him and he needs to continue to work. Um, but I think if you can get a guy that can do both in this day and age, especially on third down when it's All right, so we'll give you an example here to make more sense of this as I'm thinking. Um, say you want him to match up on a wide out, but that wide out goes in the slot. Now, he has a capability to go inside and they might not know, are we in man or zone because he's in the inside? Where if I just took an outside only guy and I brought him inside, they might say, "Oh, he's inside. He doesn't do that. They're only playing man coverage." Or maybe the guy on the outside doesn't have the ability to cover a slot. But now as he grows and develops, he could be a guy that I'm gonna follow you around the whole game regardless of where you are and I can do that. Does that kind of make sense? >> Thank you. >> Have you told us about like the seven on seven practices that you've had for guys who don't play a lot? Um >> have you seen the benefit of that? Where have you seen the benefit and where did you get that idea? Um, you know, it's something that Sully and I always talked about, you know, even before we got together, and we kind of joked, it's usually you talk about this stuff, but you don't implement it. So, it's just it's it's been really important to me. I think regardless where you're at, I think we're still in a developmental league. We just happen to be on a team that has a lot of developmental younger guys, but I think it's still a developmental league where you need to coach and you need to get your guys who aren't getting a lot of reps ready because eventually you want to see if you can get them ready to play and kind of grow them in your scheme and in your system and within your fundamentals and your techniques. So I think one I think for a guy like McCord for example, for him to get all those extra reps rather than just him running the scout team every week he's banking reps. So after 10 weeks, if he's doing that, that's a 100 extra reps in our offense. That's a big deal to me, right? Or if you look at a guy like uh you know, take a guy like Simpson who might not be getting as many reps. It's the same thing at corner. Um or it's like we seem to bring in a new guy every week. Well, we we got to get him going. That's the way to do it. Sundays, those are important. Get these guys practice and coach them and develop them. That's our job. Um, so we're gonna stay on it and um and do the best that we can helping the helping these young guys grow. It's fair to them, too. >> Okay. All right. Thank you.

text: What's up, guys? >> Jay, can you just take us through that first game, your debut at the NFL, uh, side, and just kind of just how it went for you, communication and everything all throughout? >> Yeah, I mean, um, like I said before, obviously wish we were able to come out with a win. There's a um there's something you're trying to be able to accomplish when you're when you're getting a play call. I think that he's been uh heavily in tune with everything, trying to be able to continue to help me prepare uh for every single situation, whether it's, you know, as we go through the week of practice or if we're talking about just on the sideline. Be able to ask him any question has been it's been great for me because I know that I have the confidence from from the veteran quarterback who uh has been playing in this who's been playing in the NFL for for quite some time now. So, um to be able to have that that confidence that I'm able to go up to and talk to him, it gives me even more confidence to go out there and make football plays. >> You're a really resilient guy. We've seen that here and also at Kansas. Um what was it like to to throw that first interception? you shook it off like it like it didn't even happen and then and then the flip side, what was it like to throw that first touchdown? >> Yeah, I mean um obviously >> your mind on those >> Yeah, when you throw interception you hate it. Obviously you're giving the ball to the other team and um especially in the first quarter like it's the first quarter there's still three quarters of football that need to be played and one one bad decision does not define the entire game especially that early on. And uh as a offense every single time you go out there on the field you're not thinking all right but let's punt let's let's get three. You have to um treat it, it's an opportunity that you get to go out there and be able to play against some of the best football players in the entire world. So, uh going to take it all in. Um, I don't know what his numbers are. I mean, there I thought we had a great game in the Arizona game. He carried it well last game. Obviously, the Washington game, we as a team, we didn't run it as well as we wanted to. Uh, he's a good back, man. He's he's falls forward. Um, he's got good vision. Just keep it rolling, you know. Um, we also have we have other good backs, too. I mean, uh, George has done a nice job. Bailis has a lot of speed that he's a lot he brings a lot of things to the table as well. So, uh, Emanuel's done a great job, but it doesn't just have to be him right now. >> Open the practice window for Irv Charles. Just where could he fit into things once he gets up and going? >> Yeah. Uh, I here's a physical guy. He's a big receiver. He's a great gunner. Grabwell, you know, really kind of cheering him on, so to speak. Obviously, this defense is so connected. When you hear something like that, like how cool is it >> talking about Derek on the last play? >> Well, I think the way the game went just to for us to stick together is really important, coaches included. So, then we can kind of get back on track. And I think that's a great example of of uh of our team is with all the things that were going on be able to kind of regroup in a two-minute to win the game and be able to close it out that way is um speaks a lot about our guys. >> Obviously there are penalties in your game but they're really up around the league too. Is there something you can >> I'm not I'm not sure Bob I I it's hard to it's hard to like it's hard to understand what else is going. It's like we're kind of coaches we're kind of crazy. We kind of just focus on our it's hard to get a temperature for the rest of the league. Um Brian might have a better answer for you. I think it's a know the rules and play by them better than anybody else type of thing. Like is there an, you know, certain crews have a propensity to call certain things a little bit more than others? That's something we definitely want to be aware of, you know, understanding how they're calling certain things, you know, so the guys when they understand they're in those situations how how they can play clean football. I think all that stuff helps. Um, but I mean we just we got to focus on playing great football and then the penalty stuff will take care of itself. Sometime we'll get we're going to have penalties like you know um I I don't think every team that led the league in penalties won the most games every year and I don't think the vice versa is true either. This hasn't been a month of games Brian Flurry would have envisioned losing his starting quarterback right away, losing your starting tail back. How's he navigated that? title: Cooper Kupp On The Offense Through Four Weeks "We Have A Lot Of Potential" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Hello everyone. [clears throat] >> We've talked about the smaller sample sizes the last few weeks. Is now the time where teams have declared who they are and and you can trust and and I realize it's a division opponent. You know exactly what the 49ers are going to do, but how does it change game prep? Yeah, you know, I think there's uh you definitely have enough to look at um at least what people are um are trying to be through the first, you know, uh first quarter of the season. Um but it's, you know, it's a changing league. There's always going to be new stuff, new things here and there, but um definitely nice to have a good chunk of film to go off of. >> What's it like preparing for an opponent that uh has a defensive coordinator that was a defensive coordinator for a team that you played on? >> Mhm. Yeah. No, I mean, I love Raheem. Um, great dude. Um, a great coach. Um, he's got some, you know, he's got a little bit of his, uh, his flavor. Um, in terms of what those guys are doing over there, um, it's good, it's good. I That's a really good team. Really good team. A lot of good players. U, good schemes on um, both sides of the ball. Special teams as well. And, um, going to be a great challenge for us. So, um, it'll be fun to see fun to see RAW. Um, and then, uh, going to be a going to be a great game. They don't blitz very much and they limit explosives. Uh how do they do that and and while not getting pressure uh at the same time? >> Yeah. Well, um I mean in some ways like you're if you aren't going to pressure a ton, you um you're less you got more guys in coverage, you know, you got you know, so in some ways, you know, if you're going to play the if you're going to blitz is a little more risky, a little more chance of some of the explosives coming alive. screen game can kind of come alive against some of that stuff and you get those things blocked up, you got, you know, one less guy in coverage. So, um I think that's one way that they do limit it is by being able to play coverage as much as they do. Um and then they do a good job. I mean, the safeties play a good job keeping a a shelf on top of the defense and um and guys just fly around. I think at the end of the day, there's just a level of hustle that you see on film. Um and uh yeah, that's goes guys have been like that for a long time. So, um you know, they play hard and and play together. So, uh, when you have a defense that does that, you're going to you're going to play some, uh, some efficient defense. >> So, Rasheed, get a couple carries out of the back field. Just when you have an athlete like that, how much do you like just find seeing ways to get him the ball in his hands any way possible? >> Yeah, I mean, he's explosive. He's got the ball in his hands. He can, uh, he can go. And so, um, you know, I think that's that was a cool thing to see that come alive a little bit. And, um, you know, I think, uh, you see it in the return game what he can do. So, just find ways to get the ball in his hands, I think is a is a good thing for the Seahawks. some of the outside conversations are [clears throat] it's easy to look at this point of the season compared to last year's team and I know you guys have talked about it's a new year based on your experience is this about the time where you have to go back to not making those comparisons and safeguarding against the conversations >> uh yeah I mean I think that's uh yeah I I don't know that anyone you know we get asked about it during our media sessions you know about last year but in terms of our day-to-day life like that's not what we talk out and um you know it's what are we doing on a day-to-day basis? What are we doing um week to week in terms of our our process and um you know there's no comparison game going backwards is how can we be the best Seahawks today and um it doesn't really matter at all what happened last year. Um you know it just it's about the guys that sit in this room in the mornings and um putting a plan together to go out there and execute and um yeah and that's it. What do guys like Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw do that nobody else can do uh in terms of limiting offensive options? >> Um yeah, I mean shoot both those guys um they fly around and like I said the energy um the anticipation of some of those things to being able to pattern match a lot of stuff in the coverage. Um, you know, Fred for a long time has um has patrolled the middle of the field for the 49ers and um he does a great job in coverage being able to cancel a lot of routes that you think are there based on what the coverage is giving you and he does a great job you know altering up where his drops are based on what he's seeing underneath. Um and you know that's why he's one of the best in the game. Um has been doing it for for a long time now. So it's great to see him back out there. Um but those guys I mean and you know Dre's Dre's uh been Fred's buddy for a long time. Um, and you know, Dre plays extremely hard. He's he's a physical football player. Um, you know, in in some of the same ways that Fred plays the game, um, Dre's right there with him. So, um, those two guys, um, they're going to be a great challenge. It's going to be one of those games you bring a hard hat, get ready to go. >> As a receiver, when you're playing a defense that is consistently dropping seven or eight back in coverage, what do you have to emphasize more as a receiver to be able to get open when they're having more guys back there and go? Yeah, I I think it's more about just executing your job. You know, understanding where the space is. Um there there's not uh you know, there's there's some teams that try to do it. They try to trick you and show you a bunch of different stuff that's happening. And you know, the Niners historically haven't been that way. They you kind of can kind of have a feel as the play starts. You have a good feel for where things are going to be. And then understanding that and distributing the field the right way and and then just being able to react and you got to play football because uh you know, they get a say in things too and um they have a feel for where we're going. And like I said, all those guys underneath, even the safeties and stuff, they do a really good job in terms of pattern match stuff and, um, altering drops based on the routes that we're running. And so, um, get to your spots and then be able to, you know, read and react and and go play ball. >> Four games in, what is the Seahawks offense? How would you describe it? >> What is our Seahawks offense after four weeks in? >> Um, you know, I I mean, I'd say, you know, we've got a lot of potential. um we haven't done a good enough job stringing drives together. We've, you know, left a lot of things on the table. We've made a lot of mistakes. Um you know, but I think it's a very hungry offense uh that that guys that want to find a way to um to get better and the expectation is to score every time we get on the field. And um you know, there's uh you know, when you've got the right mentality, you got the right guys, uh you know, you're going to find a way to make these things come alive. and see guys just chomping at the bit to make that you make that happen. >> Uh your weekly Brian Flurry question out of me. What what do you remember about the first meeting you guys had as an offense in the offseason? >> What I remember the first meeting we had >> first offensive meeting. >> I couldn't I couldn't even tell you what our first meeting was. So I I have no idea. That was in in April first offensive meeting. I mean, I'm sure it was something about what our identity is going to be like and in terms of getting our, you know, physicality and things that we want to um be about. Um, and he probably got quickly into the install. He doesn't want to sit up there and talk too much. He just, you know, he's about, uh, about his business. >> What was your first impression of him? >> Brian, uh, I mean, he's a very intelligent coach. He has a lot of, um, he's got a lot of knowledge about the game of football. Um, and that was very clear. Uh, from the beginning, >> we we saw you on Hard Knocks like you're in Mike McDonald's office watching film with him. Do do you kind of have that same like do you do the same thing with Brian? >> Um, yeah, here and there. It's just, you know, it's uh it's a mixed bag, you know. Um, I, you know, I try to contribute everywhere I can, try to be an asset wherever I can. Um, and, uh, yeah, we got a lot of a lot of guys in this office. I play a lot of football. So, um, wherever we can, you know, feel like we can, you know, share an opinion here or there, um, you guys are willing to do that. >> Was it that way for you in Los Angeles, too? Like bouncing meeting to meeting. It's not just the wide receiver rooms or McDonald, but we saw you in all sorts of rooms. Like, when did that all kind of start for you? >> Um, yeah, I think it's kind of been that way. Um, just trying to be around. I think at the end of the day, like I said, you just you want to try to find a way to affect games. You want to be a part of something that, you know, allows guys to play to their best ability. You want to see plays come alive. And um No, it's like it's it's why you play this game, you know, it's why why I play this game is to um have a hand in us walking off that field on Sunday with a W. And it doesn't have to be because the ball was in my hands. It can be because I had something to say to someone that, you know, helped them come alive on a play. And um you know, it helps the Seahawks. So, um, you know, I'm always going to be that way, and there's a lot of guys in this building that are that way. You know, whatever they can do to help move things forward is what we're about. >> Whenever this ride is over, is coaching on the horizon for you? And is this something you've ever really thought of? >> I'm not really thinking about it right now. >> There was obviously a lot of penalties in your game last week, but there's the penalties are up around the league as well, kind of a pretty uh pretty pretty high over the last couple decades as play. Have you noticed that as players like they're calling certain things differently or tight or anything tighter or anything like that or? >> Yeah, you know, I don't know. It's hard to tell. I think there's uh I think in some ways you get to a point where you know the rules have become there's a lot those refs are out there looking at. There's a lot that they have to see. Um and the amount of rules and verbiage that's going through their heads, you know, at the snap of a fingers. It's a lot. And so I think, you know, in some ways you get to the point where like people have been playing football for a long time, watching football for a long time, you see it and you're like, "Oh, I know what that is." But when you're on the field in the moment, having to see it in real time and decipher through all the verbiage of the uh NFL rule book, I think it can be a little tough. And so those guys are in a tough spot. They're in a really tough position. And we all get the um courtesy of being able to see things in slow motion after the fact and things like that. So, um I think they're doing the best job they can and um you know, we're just going to keep um I know like they come in here on in during uh training camp, you know, we get a good, you know, few days we'll talk to them. You know, they don't want to be they don't want to be the ones that the campers on. You know, they they want to see uh good football u being played the right way. So, um I know all that stuff's going to get worked out. >> Two two long touchdown in this game, both finished with a receiver blocking at the end of the play. you on the screen pass, Jack's on the on Rashid's on. Is that something when coaches are showing film Monday that they highlight, you know, Jax is down there taking a safety out, things like that? >> Yeah. No, it's something that we talk about all the time. So, um, you know, the things that coaches emphasize are the things that, you know, we try make sure we make sure we bring those things alive and, um, and yeah, when guys do that, when, you know, when you see jacks running across the field making a, you know, touchdown a touchdown saving block on the opposite corner, um, yeah, you're going to you're going to see it on on on tape on Monday. >> Teams that you've been on throughout your career that have excelled in third down, what what are some common traits there and what are some of the most important factors when it comes to executing on third down? Yeah, I think there's one clarity of um clarity of your of your job, I think, is is the first thing. So, you got to be able to play um and react knowing that on third down, you're going to get a lot of historically against, you know, NFL teams, you're going to get a lot of mixed up stuff. You're going to get some weird looks. You know, you're get some exotic pressures and things like that. And so, um you know, as as an offense, you want to make sure there's clarity of what you need to get done. Um so, you can, you know, execute what needs to happen as all these things are moving and shifting. clarity of rules so you can solve the problems out there because the coach isn't going to be in your ear telling you what you're supposed to do on this look, you know. So, um having those the clarity of what you're going to get done, those those rules, problem solve, um and then just being able to play decisive, um you know, be able to react to zone, anticipate things you're supposed to. There's there's a lot of things that go into it, but um third downs, I think, are a lot about the preparation you have during the week, um and be able to have answers for whatever it's going to be and then allowing just guys to to play decisively on Sunday. Awesome. Thank you guys.

text: That's okay. What's up, guys? Um, all right. Injuries for today. James Thompson ankle won't practice. Bosa calf won't practice. Juice knee won't practice. Seagull ankle won't practice. I didn't get done till halftime, but >> were you not into it? No, not really. Not at all. It was tough. >> What have you seen from Brian Flurry's offensive scheme and what he's done up there? >> Um, I mean, I think he's taken over where Clint left off. Just I'm running a similar scheme. Doing a really good job. Uh, especially with the challenge of their backs getting hurt. Um, but Brian's a guy that knows the run game really well. Um, puts on a does a really good scheme with that and doing a hell of a job getting the ball. It's in Jigba. How easy is it to kind of forget about that if you come into a new season, you're going up against the very team that was celebrating? >> Uh, very easy. Um, not I mean, it's just a it's a feel like with us it's we don't totally get into that outer stuff very much. I mean, every game is so tough, no matter who you play, and you don't really attach years before to certain games.
