text: Morning everyone. Mike, >> what did you see on that CVY front return uh down to the inside the 20? What what does he do well and what did what did he show you on that play? >> Yeah. Uh CVY is doing what he done since I've seen him, you know, play at Utah. He does a really good job of kind of setting up the return, making the first guy missed. Um he does a great job of kind of after he beats that first wave of understand to get downhill. And you know, it's tougher on on the coverage team when somebody's almost playing, you know, a little little game of chicken with you which way he's going to go and he's so shifty in terms of that. Um, but again, it it doesn't really the returns don't start without the help of all the other 10 guys in front of him. Um, you know, Kenny Moore and Jay Jones, veteran guys, they did a heck of a job on that vice on the left side. I don't think the gunner got past the 15 yd line. You know, key, we put a lot on on Keely's plate to to get the return started. Then Josiah had a great block coming back leading with his hands to kind of almost take out two guys with his block. Kind of took out the unblock guy we left run free. Then you know CVY kind of did the rest on himself. And you know you see a lot of guys that that'll run out of bounds after they get certain. He's not looking to run out of bounds. He's trying to get that cut back to get more yards which you could you could really appreciate. Um and you know that was just really good complimentary football to go from you know a backed up punt defense three and out big return then to a touchdown. You know, that's that's what makes football just the ultimate team game. >> Sideline, what do you think about your options return? >> Yeah, I mean, we've we've obviously shuffled some guys around depending on on week to week and like I said last week to week to week basis. Um, we're going to look into all of our options. You know, obviously CVY's one of them. He's been a kickoff returner for us um in the past and we have we have some great guys that are in this room on this roster that have had some experience doing it. So again, we're going to we're going to rely on everybody. You know, the 53, the 63 with the practice squad, you know, it's always going to be a a full full uh cohort effort this week. >> What's a week like this like though when you have so many injuries and obviously there's a big trickle down to special teams. >> Yeah, you know, everybody's got problems. Everybody's got professional problems. Everybody's got personal problems. Jacksonville don't care about our problems. So we're not going to dwell on it. That's going not going to be wo is me. It's going to be everybody that sits in this room. And I told them Monday after we cleaned up the tape against uh the Rams, it's going to be everybody, you know, hand in hand, lock step to get this the right way we want. Um, so again, it's not just one person or or two people. It's going to be the entirety of the team to to help out. You may see some guys that have a majority role on offense or defense have to play a couple roles, but it is what it is. That's what we do. That's what we do in special teams. We rely on everybody. And, you know, I think the guys just want to have the best results possible, so they'll do what they can moving forward. see to see Jake hit the the uh 56 yard. He's two for two on 50 yarders this year. I mean, what does that say about him and and you know, how he's how he's doing so far. >> Yeah, I mean, I think that just shows how strong mentally he is still physically, how how gifted he is as a kicker. And again, I can't speak for how Jake feels about it. You'd have to ask him, but for me, I've never lost that confidence. I see him every day when we're out on the practice field, you know, putting in the work, grinding it out, you know, not just working on his field goals, but also his kickoffs to help out the team any way he can. And, you know, I've always said it, I think, for years now that I could talk about him, Braden, now Rocco for for hours on end. So for him, I think it's just one of those things that you just see him, you know, have that mental fortitude to go out there and some tough conditions, wet, windy, and and you know, his number was called and he answered the bell. >> What another inside of 10 for Braden? What's his preparation like behind the scenes just to get to those results? >> Yeah. Um, I've never seen a punter punt more than Braden Mann does from a week- toeek basis, but he is so, you know, everybody talks about being, you know, a critic. Nobody's a bigger critic on themselves than Braden Man, and he's going to work out what he needs to work out throughout the entirety. And it's kudos to him. Um, you know, also shout out my guy Nick Still on Thursdays. He's the equipment guy that he shags for for Braden regardless. We'll have to get him a uh a cave helmet with a light as the the lights kind of dwindle down, but he just works his tail off from Wednesday through Friday, getting everything dialed in, how he likes it, what what we talk about, how we want to approach the game. And again, like like I said, you know, watching him prepare is pretty awesome. That's what you like about coaching is seeing how these guys get to a week-toeek basis on on game day. And, you know, it's more kudos to him how he performs on Sunday, Monday, whatever it is. >> How many points would you estimate, >> brother? So that that number is infinite. Infinite. I have no clue. I gave up on that that probably four weeks when we got him in 23. I was like, you know what? Whatever gets you to Sunday, I'm going to back up every time. >> Going back to Cubby, he he uh looked like there was a time in the game that he fielded a punt. Gunnar was standing in his face. He didn't fair catch it. Got a few yards, I think. Uh what do you like to see in that situation? You okay with him not calling a fair catch there? >> Yeah, I've been around C now long. not going to second guess his decision-m. You know, everything's not, you know, cookie cutter. Not everything's black and white. I think it's more of him having that such trust on Keley on the one-on-one out there that he's going to get any gunner out there stop. Um, but again, I'm never going to second guess what they do in the game. I'm not the one in between the white lines. You know, we we build that trust through the practice, through different scenarios, different situations. Um, and again, that's more of a a question for him to have his what his thought process is. For me, it's like he secured the ball, he got a couple yards, went down, secured it. In that in that case, you know, if he doesn't catch the ball, who knows what that ball does if it bounces and now goes inside the 15. Um, so again, it's just more of that that trust I have in CVY, the trust he has in Keley and the other guys blocking for him. And again, everything's, you know, hindsight 2020 after you see it on the film. But I I'll never be one to to second guess. It's more of just, you know, a learning then talk about it then move on to the next play because it it happens fast. >> Circumstance might mean Will has a larger role in the offense this week. He does a lot for you. Um, how does that week go? I know you're not going to tell, but how does that week go? How quickly do you know you're going to have his normal role or how does that sort of develop? Yeah, I'm also never going to put the players in a disadvant disadvantage in their scenario. You know, if he happens to be the the lead bellcow, that would be selfish of me to ask him to do whatever he has to do on special teams. But that's why football's the ultimate team game. That's why we're going to rely on other guys that may have to um kind of carry that load that he had as a four core, you know, guy we rely on. But that's what we do from the beginning of OTAAS to training camp to now is train everybody to do multiple different things. You'll see some guys out there. I mean at the last punt you saw Jay Hunt out there at the wing when tank went down. It's just a very unselfish move from these guys. Um and they know we could we could trust those guys in those scenarios. So again it's going to be a full team effort to kind of mitigate some of the things that happen. You know injuries as part of the game but we're going to rely on a whole bunch of different people. We're going to rely on our guys that that perform at a high level. I thought Keley and Smile did a great job bouncing back after the Monday night game. I think Smile had two tackles, solo tackles and two assisted tackles. Keely had one solo and two assisted. You know, those production guys, you know, they're going to have to step up and we know we can rely on them. So, it's going to be a full team effort to kind of mitigate all the the stuff that happens with injuries. >> What's the scouting report on the Jaguar special teams? >> Yeah, very very good unit. Um Heath obviously played in the NFL for a long time. They carry, you know, like I talked about with Bubba last week, um they carry the same type of tenacity that he played with as a former player. Obviously, Parker Washington is a dangerous punt returner. I think he had two touchdowns last year and also had a 43 yard last year. I think he actually had one called back, so that would have made three. Um he's quick. Um he's got home run hitting ability. You know, Logan Cook and and Cam Little, they're very very good specialists. You know, Logan Cook, I think, has every kick in the bag, banana ball, regular pull hook. You know, he he's been doing it for a long time. And a guy that I don't think, you know, I think he has the respect in the special teams world, but that's probably looked over as Ross Matis. I think he's probably one of the best coverage long snappers, one of the better athletes out there. So, you know, when you get out there on pump return, you usually kind of let the long snapper run free. You got to count him in the box because I think he has 24 career tackles as a long snapper. So, we got our hands full. Um, you know, we're developing that game plan. almost done with that. Then, you know, send it out to the players tonight. Then, you know, it it's back to work tomorrow. Um, starting with punt and kickoff return and and, you know, get a a nice jump on the on the week and, you know, be ready to go go play in London. >> Penalty was >> what's your view of international games and is it is it something you look forward to or is it just a long flight in the game for you? >> Yeah, it's a free vacation to a different continent. That's that that's it for me. But, it's all business more than anything else. You know, I've been fortunate enough in my offseason to visit London. Love London. I think it's a really cool place. You know, a lot of different things, but for us, this is solely a business trip and, you know, we got to we got to be able to go out there and regardless of where they put that ball down, we got to be able to go out there and help the team win any way we can. >> Have you been in the Hopper Hot Stadium before? And do you um do any pre kind of uh work or talk talk to other special teams coordinators in the offseason in terms of kicking there, punting there? >> Not not necessarily. Um, never I mean I haven't been to Hotspur Stadium. I've been to Arsenal. I've been to Man City. Um, just in different travels. But, you know, me and Tyler, we kind of look at how it's kind of constructed the stadium. And, you know, I think the cool thing about soccer stadiums is they create the elements by just having the the top open right there. Then the fans are covered up, which I think is a really cool concept for soccer and everything like that. So, that kind of mitigates a little bit of the wind if there is wind. Um, so and you know there's so many now filmed games of you know being in Tottenham uh stadium that you could kind of see you know there's a little bit of a sunlight and shadows last week with uh Indianapolis and Washington. So you always take that into effect but for the most part you know we're just like anybody else looking at the weather every every day and go off that. >> On that Keely penalty was he anticipating them to make the first contact and how do you coach that? Yeah, it's just one of those things where you do try to anticipate and we have, you know, we try to tell them, hey, we want to run the sideline hash. Usually when that happens and you take that up field on the sideline hash, they're going to have to contact you. It's one of those things that we can't have because it puts everybody else at risk. You know, with that second punt and you just ran, shoot 50 yards as fast as you can and they have to bring you back. That puts a lot of uh strain on the rest of the the punt team. Um something we could learn off and coach off of. But I thought Braden did a heck of a job coming back with a 49 yard out of bounds to kind of, you know, take it upon himself and help everybody else out cuz again that that's an extra strain on on the team. But, you know, something we can learn off of and something that he he'll learn off of and correct. But it's one of those things where we we can't put a how do I want to say this? Non-physical penalty out there. Something that we know that we can't do uh able to to overcome it, but we can't have any more of those. >> Michael, one more on on CVY. He's a lot of a lot of returners would rather fair catch or let a ball go out of bounds to protect their average. He doesn't seem to care about that. He's like he he'd rather get three yards than have a you know no return to protect his average. What does that say about him? >> That is he's one of the more unselfish players that you that you could be about and you know those three yards those six yards they may come in handy at some point. You know a 38 yarder that's bouncing the ball and you only get four yards shoot that net's 34 you're going to be in far better field possession. And it just, you know, understanding the whole complexities of the game, not just protecting your your stats or like that cuz, you know, the more often that he's able to get returns just like he did in that game, his average will be just fine, but it's more of what am I going to do to help the team in that particular instance for the game, which you can always respect, you know, as a teammate, as a coach, manto man, that he's going to do something that's unselfish, that's going to be for the betterment of the team. >> I could follow up on Will Shipley. I know obviously you might not have him as much as as typically, but what what is his value to your special teams unit? I mean, I know he's off all four core and everything. Just what he means. >> Yeah, you know, getting Will our first year in 24 and a rookie being a personal protector that puts a lot of strain on him, but I thought he did a great job of understanding what his role was. Then he's just kind of taken that leadership role over the last two and a half, three years. Um Will, you know, during the week, he's a very, you know, calm, cool, collected cat. Really doesn't get too high, but he brings that fire and desire on game days. You know, if something's not right, he will let somebody know that it's not right. Um, which we kind of we kind of like and and see out of him. Um, he does it in practice. If he doesn't if something happens, you know, on punt pro and we miss something, he was not afraid to get on his teammates. And you got to respect that. a guy that's able to do that and and care so much about it. It's not just the person he is helping correct. It's the entirety of the unit saying this is a player run um special teams unit we try to involve. So if he says something, he's the captain of the unit. We we go with that. So, I think, you know, and I don't think we'll lose any of that because he'll sit in this room, you know, the next couple days. And, you know, any input or help out anybody that may be taking his place on uh on the on the uh units, he's going to be more than happy to to help and get them ready for Sunday. >> Mention Rock is now a guy that you can talk about hours on and what what stood out to you about him in the first four weeks as a part of the operation, how he's grown up as the long snapper. >> Yeah, usually when you don't talk about the long snapper for the first four games, he's doing a pretty good job. Um, I thought he had one of his best snaps in that 56 yard field goal in the in the rain with the win. I mean, he threw perfect laces, perfect height. Braden, all I had to do was pick uh catch it and put it down. And he's just he's just maturing. He's improving on everything. We still don't give him easy looks on practice. We're going to make it as hard as we can possibly. And that's a kudos to the practice squad guys, you know, James Newbie, Mason Rager, like those guys give him such great looks that when it comes to the game, it comes so naturally to him and maybe even slowed down a little bit. So for him to keep improving, you know, his footwork, you know, his strength, moving guys out. He, you know, he had go against Brandon Fisk a couple times on pump return. He did a good job, you know, of using his technique, running his feet, kicking his hip, getting them wide right there. So, we're still going to make it extremely hard for Roco, but he's doing a really good job thus far. >> Nick has said several times, including this morning, that he he coaches his coaches really hard. Um, how do you feel that? Yeah, I mean you don't want to be, you know, kind of coddled, you know, you never want to be coddled in life. You know, when he demands something, he demands something. And it's on on us as manto man to to fill that void for whatever he asks. You know, I rather have somebody chew me out than kind of go backwards and kind of be, you know, lz fair with it. Um, but you know, you can only respect somebody that that you report to and you want to give all you all all you can for him in terms of just as the head coach, the organization to be able to put our our right foot forward and help the team out we possibly can from a special teams unit. >> Great. Thanks. Thanks, man.

title: Inside The Tape With Greg Cosell: "Everything Changed When Mitchell Went Out"

With me is Adam Kaplan, and of course Greg Cosell, to continue our analysis of the Eagles' 24-20 loss to the Rams on Sunday in the fourth round.  In the last episode, we analyzed the offensive game.  Now, Greg, we have to deal with the consequences of a defense that finally, finally threw a few interceptions, kind of carried the offense for about two and a half to three quarters, and then when it came down to it at the end, they just ran out of key players and ran out of steam.  But what was your overall impression of the defense for most of the game until that last stretch? You know, it's funny. Believe it or not, it seemed to me that everything changed to some extent when Mitchell was eliminated , and it happened on the very first play of the second half.  Um, and then, just a few plays later, Devante Adams just beat Jones when they were playing "cover-1" and Stafford just rolled him over.  And I think that scared Vic.  I think Vic felt: you know what?  I do n't know how much " cover-1" I can use. So when Jones came out , and he's only about 5'10", how did he Rams' big wide receivers? title: QB Jayden Daniels Speaks To The Media After Practice | Washington Commanders
text: to play with the brace on and kind of protect yourself while also obviously being able to play the game, you know? >> Nah. Uh I Yeah. No, I can't uh really I mean just ways you could talk about different ways of protecting myself. Um but I don't I don't get hit in practice, so I wouldn't know till Sunday. Knowing everything you've been through over the last year or so, was it different for you in London watching Marcus go down and then knowing you couldn't go in to try to help your team? >> Um, yeah. I mean, as a competitor, you want to go out there and help your team win. Um, and that was an unfortunate circumstance. Uh, just the way the game was going and how Marcus was playing up to that point. And you never want to see anybody deal with injuries like that. um you know I felt felt for him in in that sense because obviously you know I was going through the same thing and um you know unfortunately I was the same one that he was dealing with earlier. So uh it's just unfortunate but at that point it was like I was just shifting all my focus and energy into um you know uplifting Aan um and making sure that he can go out there and play free and you know just giving him those things that I see. Not trying to overdo too much but um just help him out any way I can. And then knowing every game's important, but seeing where this team is, another division game, how much do you measure we've got to get a win here versus take every week on its own? >> Um, I mean, this week is the the game that we have, so obviously, you know, we want to get a win and uh we got a tough divisional opponent coming in and uh we know what's at stake, but uh you just got to go out there and take it day by day, play by play. um and you know try to execute to the best of our abilities. >> Uh Jaden, as you know, you know, injuries, there's situations where you can play through it, maybe not be yourself. What gave you the confidence as you were getting evaluated and meeting with those consultants that you can not only come back and play, but be you when you're back out there? >> Um it's my non-throwing arm. So, uh I think as long as I got the right one to attack, you know, I think I can I'll be all right. And then for you guys overall as offense, just because of you being in and out and other guys getting injured, you haven't been able to really be in a rhythm. Um, we saw it a little bit early against the Cowboys, but how confident are you in the ability of of you to kind of get back up to speed quickly this week? >> I'm super confident. I mean, you know, just putting in the countless hours of work and preparation. I just go out there and give myself the best opportunity to perform to the best of my abilities on Sunday. Um, so, you know, just taking it day by day really. Um, Jaden, we've talked about the brace and, you know, physically what's been going on, but like mentally, emotionally, spiritually, like where are you at coming back from an injury after experiencing what you did last year and what you've learned from last year to take into this year? >> I'm straight. Honestly, I'm good. Uh, you know, I was kind of Last year was a a different thing for me. This time, I kind of just knew what was at stake. Went to all the different specialists and heard the opinions and, you know, kind of based my decision off of there. um you know, prayed about it, you know, make sure I'm making the best decision. I was at peace. I was at peace with it. >> Jaden, is there anything you learned in the Minnesota game? I know it's a different brace, but anything you learned from that experience that could help you now? >> Nah. Go out there and play ball. No, not really. >> And you know, just how how has it felt just moving around out there? I know maybe somebody asked about already. Is there any um anything where you still are adjusting to anything with the brace? Uh, no. I mean, just trying to get used to it, like I said. Um, it's kind of a part of me now. So, you know, for the time being, as long as I'm on that field, so just getting used to it, you know, trying to find the different ways where it's most comfortable and I'm not really just thinking about I'm just out there playing. >> Hey, Jaden. Coach Quinn talked about maybe trying to instill some running back technique as you carry the ball when you get out of the pocket. I wonder is that feeling natural or how's it been adjusting to to that style of carrying the ball when you get out? I ain't carried the ball yet, so we'll see. But yeah, we talked about it. >> Just curious, last year in Minnesota when you had the brace for the first time then and it was a different brace. Just kind of watching you in warm-ups, it clearly felt like maybe annoying or cumbersome or something. Do you have a different mental approach this time with the brace? >> Hell yeah. I want to play football, so it's a part of me. So, got to go out there and embody embrace it. Does it feel does this one feel more comfortable for you? >> Uh, we still trying to figure out the most comfortable way for me to go out there and not play. So, he's still making critiques and everything to it. Uh, trying to find the best way for it. >> Along those lines, is that what you mean when you say this one's different? Just the fact that you kind of gone through what this process is like or is it something else that feels different? >> Um, I mean, yeah, I went through the process um and it wasn't, you know, the end of everything. Um, like I said, I was blessed enough to, you know, still be allowed to play this game and, uh, you know, I'm just going to go out there. I'm embrace it. I'm embrace the brace. Um, not really worry too much about it and go out there and just be the best version of myself. >> Uh, one on the field question. You've managed to get the ball to Terry and to Diggs and to Williams. Um, and so is Marcus. Um, do you think it's an issue that the tight ends haven't been as involved yet? And do you think that there's a way to incorporate them into the game plan more or is it just the guy's open, he gets the ball? >> The guy's open, gets the ball. Um, you know, we had, you can see we dealt with a lot of different injuries and, you know, stuff like that up to this point. Um, you know, where people are in and out of the lineup and and stuff like that. And obviously, I think teams do a good job of covering our tight ends, too. So, uh, these other guys one-on-one outside and they win too. But, uh, we just out here just playing point guard, trying to get the ball to the open guy. >> Anybody else? >> Appreciate y'all.

title: HC Dan Quinn Speaks To The Media Before Practice | Washington Commanders
text: fill you in a little bit what I discussed with the staff um also today and or not today but last night as we're hitting you know the early part of the season um so much is about us and even more so than the opponents and uh sometimes the early new schemes new play callers uh but really just trying to get our football right and uh we've definitely had some moving parts for sure I told them but uh this week I wanted to make sure our emphasis was on our mental discipline our pre- snap penalties and we have got to get that right and uh added some officials for practice, but I wanted definitely our our focus on that for sure. So, yes, big division game, but if you walked inside in the halls right now, I think you'd feel urgency, energy, uh to play like us, period. Fast, aggressive, and playing cleaner. And uh that's not opponent driven, that's us driven. And uh we're ready to get rolling. We're excited that we activated uh the 21day windows on uh Trey and Dietrich and Jmack. and it'll be great to have them back out at practice. They've worked extremely hard through the rehab process and so it' be good to have them back to it. So, all that said, ready to get rolling with you guys. >> Dan, I know you emphasize winning time moments often, you know, third downs, fourth downs, u you know, also having um you know, fourth fourth quarter situations, late game situations. How do you think you guys can be better on both sides of the ball in those areas? >> Yep. I thought um I've liked over the last couple weeks the third down, there's been improvement on that side for sure. Um, and so each week you're kind of all right, where are the markers of what you wanted to hit? What targets did you want to hit? Somebody just won a drinking contest right there. I just saw. So that's good. I saw there was the comment markers. I'm trying to get them out, you guys. Honestly, let's have some fun with that. Um, as we're going through the situations, I want to make sure that we deal them in practice. Might have been a red zone one, might have been a fourth down op, might have been a third down op. It might have been, you know, a scenario in the two-minute piece that we like. So, we try to hit those as often as we can. I liked how we did some in Seattle. Um, didn't love the end of the half this week. So, it's constantly one that we're digging in on. And as we get through it, there'll be, you know, kind of ones that I like, ones I don't, but it's on the front of my mind almost every week, every game. >> With Terry McLaren, I know, you know, his stats has kind of been up in the air with that hamstring injury. Do you have any update on where he's at? >> He will work off to the side today and we'll have a, you know, better reportage getting through to tomorrow and Friday. >> Morning, Dan. Uh, where do you see the disconnect with the tight ends in the passing game? It hasn't really been activated all season like where do you see >> the lacking I guess there? >> I'm hopeful that one, like talking about Chick specifically, that he and Jay have spent like all of training camp working through together. So, that's a big deal. We didn't get as much of that so far this season. Uh certainly felt like he had, you know, part of the plan a little bit got derailed in this last game, but going into it, um having him back out at practice, back into the mix, I uh definitely see that trend going up. >> Dan, when you look at the second half defense against the Colts and really just the whole season so far, do you feel like the defense is wearing down as the game goes on or how do you kind of assess how the defense has finished games and do you like it or not? Yeah, I definitely want the uh the response, you know, in the toughest spots to go nail it. And uh in the third quarter, I think there was a drive for a touchdown, one that, you know, was a field goal maybe on a shorter field. But that's definitely one of the topics that we've hit on. I love the energy that we start with, but for sure the second half has been something that uh defensively we've had a lot of conversations about, you know, over the last couple days and finding our ways to respond like in those strongest moments at the ends of the game for us. And uh that was definitely one that like is at the high part of our list. I've liked the third down improvement, communication improvement, a number of things. So those would be the next step for me is seeing that response um when it's time to go close the door. >> Dan, Dan, with Jaden, um how much you talked about if he plays protecting that elbow, how do you go about that and how much do you talk with it so it doesn't get too much in his head, but he's cognizant of it? It's a good topic and uh the best way I explained it to him and um if he's you know normally scrambling slides when to throw it out if but you know in a group you know think of it like a running back who class the ball you know rolling to the ground. So I thought of him as that player and that's the way we explained it and those are like honestly just some practice drills that we'll be doing today. Um but it's definitely something we talk about. We're going to practice it and like this is him moving forward and how we'll play. >> And then with Marcus no IR. So, how optimistic are you about maybe returning in a couple weeks and how much of that factor in maybe not bringing someone else in from the outside? >> We're optimistic that the injury was similar that hopefully they'll follow the same plan for him and if we can do that, that would mean sooner than later, meaning another game and a buy. So, we're encouraged about what his return could look like. Yeah. >> Um, >> with Trey, just given the fact that he's only really had one full practice since the injury last November, >> correct? >> How fast can you get him up to speed? Like what do you have to take extra precautions given that timetable? >> Not extra. Um, Austin Eckler ruined it for everybody. So, practice is important, Nikki. I think that's the main thing with Jeremy, with Dietrich there's and Trey. So, no guidelines into it. Let's go see where we're at, play some ball. But as far as into the game, like way too early to call. Like, let's really go out and push it and then get into practice. And when the three of them, we'll kind of customize for each of them when that's the right time. >> With Mikey, have you I mean, you I know you're in the midst of the season kind of going through everything right now. Um, but are you able to kind of make sense of what led to maybe his struggles there in coverage and kind of what he needs to do to get back? >> We moved him inside to nickel and we wanted to feature him there. More often than not, if there's a focus, a thing you can fix cleanly, we will. And Mike is definitely doing that. Confidence in him is high. We know he's capable of, so we're going to continue to push him. Um, we'll lean back on him. I'm certain that we will. >> Um, do you have any sense, any better sense of Tonsil's rehab in terms of getting him back up to speed and ready to play? >> Not a timeline yet. He had the last checkup recently. They were pleased, but they're still in the process this part of the healing. It's a longer recovery in that spot, but not nothing of a timetable just yet. Um, and with regard to the to the offensive penalties that you're having, I mean, I know you want to have some continuity, but you do have the power to remove people from the field if they continue to make those mistakes. And is that something that you consider doing? >> I would definitely consider that. And I'm certain that we are going to get this fixed. Certain. We have to. There's no ifands or buts about it. So losing big plays due to a pre- snap foul and in the defensive case a post snap foul um cost us and we were going to work really hard to attack that. >> Dan, you and Adam spent most of the summer telling us how much confidence you had in Nick Aligretti, how smart of a player he is, how he's played a lot of guard, but he's really um capable at center. Y what's happened there? He's essentially been benched at both center and and guard. Yeah, I think there's a lot that goes into it. It's like most things on the discussion. I think one missing a lot of camp obviously has a factor. Uh he was also banged up to calf hip and so I am very much the conversation with him. I'm looking forward to getting Nick Aligrady ball back like his toughness and will Barry is strong and so as we're in the last week this week um I'm looking forward to seeing that technique really improve. That's that's who Nick is and uh I'm certain that we'll see that, you know, continue up. Just his kind of will and toughness uh allowed him to go, but I'm looking forward to him really getting into a good working rhythm at the position. >> Hey, coach. >> Hello. >> Uh you said that hitting the early part of the season is all about you all and not about the opponent. What are the things at this point that you're really stressing being that all of the hard work you put in doing the training camp up to this point? What are you stressing with the team? >> The first one, like we talked about earlier, was the pre-nap fouls, you know, and the discipline uh that goes in for that, Donna. That's a big piece. Different sides of the ball, different ones to go. Like looking forward to getting our run game going and establish that. I'm excited for Sam getting back into practice as well. It's been nice having EC and J-Mack back as well. And so we've got a very strong group of running backs. Um on the defensive side, there's still work to do and creating more takeaways where the last two games that's going. So in my mind, what I usually hit with the staff, myself, what do we learn and what do we got to continue to build on and where are the weaknesses that needed shoring up? And so this is that week where you kind of get into that where you can and the pre- snap fouls were my biggest one offensively. Uh let's stay on schedule, stay on track for that. Defensively, the continuation of really attacking the football. That's going to be a big piece. And then on the return side, I like how we're covering. I felt like we've, you know, not hit our kickoff returns and punt returns at the level that I think we're capable of um based on who the returners are. And in the secondary, what are what are the improvements that you're seeing there beyond the turnovers that you're starting to see take place? But when you really look at the secondary over the last couple of games, what improvements have you seen there and what improvements do you still want to see? >> I think standing here probably after the Dallas game, you guys heard me talk about communication a lot and uh that's always king defensively and I felt that part has improved over the last two games. Seattle had a lot of yards, but the improvement, there wasn't, you know, a mixup, a bust in that spot to go. I'm excited about the improvement. I'm excited that Nick Cross also is back into this mix as well, back at practice. But that alone has been significant for us. I'm looking forward to more technique, all of those things you want to constantly improve. But starting with that, that was a big step. Hey Dan. Um, you guys have basically had three quarterbacks on the active roster pretty much every week since you've been here. A couple exceptions here, including like this last week. Considering you're hopeful with Jaden and all that, but considering his injury history and the way Ethan was taking hits, is there any what's the thought with activating Sam Hartman either to the 53 or as an eleation? >> It was definitely things that we had discussed for sure um in the last week and we'll Adam and I will have those same discussions this week. Yeah. So definitely um like a lot of confidence in Sam and thought the improvement he made going into this year was the biggest jump he's made in two years and so it's definitely a conversation we've had. >> Take a good teammate. >> Good teammate. Thanks for the assist. Um you guys had a lot of injuries last year and and the season obviously ended up the way that it did as were early on in the season here. What are some of the things that you learned from that experience last year with this with what you can control that you can bring, you know, this season and and not let the not not let last year happen? >> Yeah, it's a great question and the biggest one that comes to mind for me and you've heard me say it is the 70man roster and already leaning into that through four games has been a big deal for us. and going through the injury sucks. And the silver lining that comes out of it that later on in the season, later on in football, you know, now you've got some experience with people like Goldman, you know, Kay Madano, others that have gained starting experience into it and your whole team gains a little stronger and a little more depth as you go. But I think that's the big lesson knowing that like every person here is up like the phrase in the Navy like all hands on deck. And I think that started even way back if you guys remember like in mini camp and playing more people and into the practices. So, we're gonna continue with that. >> Time for two more. >> Good. >> I'll go Ben and Nikki to end it. >> Um, with regards to the the running game, had a chance to look at some tape. So to see with Leo going down, Frankie was down, Kane step into that spot, that's a big deal. And, uh, no one deliver be counted on, like that's as important as it gets. And, uh, there'll be others that have that, so it is capable. It's not the same, but there's always a way to go. And I like that we've kind of pushed everybody along in that spot this year. >> All right. Thanks everybody.
